text:
tyler: heads up, noticed a p99 tail spike on /generate after the kernel selector change + new coalesce jitter defaults :thinking_face:

sarah: ugh, timeline? what changed exactly?

tyler: yesterday 02:40 UTC we flipped kernel-priority to prefer `amp-quant` for small seqs, and bumped `coalesce_jitter_pct` from 8 -> 18 for host pools. first spike shows up ~03:12 UTC.

priya: any KV cache metrics? could be eviction churn with the new kernel path
tyler: yes - KV hit rate dropped on the route from 0.94 -> 0.67 around the same time. bandwidth/throughput steady though.

jonathan: interesting. kernel swap could change per-token timing which influences batching windows and KV lifetime. did we change token budget targets?
tyler: token budget target still 1024, but effective microbatch interval drifted up since `amp-quant` emits longer per-token wall times. that increases queueing, so longer-lived KV entries get evicted.

siva: I ran a quick canary locally reverting jitter pct to 6% and microbatch_interval_ms to 3ms. p99 improved ~14%, p95 ~6%.

perf-bot: canary results: https://dash.redwood/canaries/2750012345 (summary: p50 18ms -> 17ms, p95 78ms -> 73ms, p99 210ms -> 180ms) :white_check_mark:

elena: can you paste the experiment config and a short perf sample?
tyler: paste below, simple diff from production:

```
# before (prod)
microbatch_interval_ms: 6
coalesce_delay_ms: 2
coalesce_jitter_pct: 18
token_budget_target: 1024
kernel_policy: [amp-quant, fp16, fp32]

# canary
microbatch_interval_ms: 3
coalesce_delay_ms: 1
coalesce_jitter_pct: 6
token_budget_target: 1024
kernel_policy: [amp-quant, fp16, fp32]
```

perf snippet from the canary host (20k requests):
```
requests: 20000
avg_tokens/sec: 14500
p50_latency_ms: 17
p95_latency_ms: 73
p99_latency_ms: 180
kv_hit_rate: 0.91
GPU_util: 62%
```

priya: kv_hit_rate jump back to 0.91 looks telling. I suspect microbatch timer increase was amplifying KV churn when combined with jitter.

jonathan: another angle: `amp-quant` kernel might be slightly slower for short sequences due to extra dequant path, nudging more requests into longer-lived KV slots. combined with larger jitter, some microbatches wait long enough to force eviction.

siva: agree. my trace showed more frequent KV slab evictions around 3–6s TTL windows. lowering interval reduces window tail so entries get reused.

elena: proposal: for rollout, pin kernel priority for the critical route to keep previous perf (fp16 preferred) and ship a tuning PR that reduces jitter for the next 48h while we validate. rollouts are cheap to revert.

tyler: +1. also want to run an ablation: keep kernel change but keep original microbatch interval and jitter to see if kernel alone causes regression.

perf-bot: created issue #INF-7843 with canary artifacts and flamegraphs: https://issues.redwood/INF-7843 :issue:

priya: could we add a short-lived metric: `batch_holdtime_p99` and `kv_slot_reuse_rate` to the routes dashboard? will help correlate quickly on future swaps.

jonathan: doing that now, pushing to staging dashboard.

siva: small sanity check: does coalesce_delay_ms=1 cause microbursts that harm kernel throughput? I ran a microbenchmark and saw no throughput loss, but GPU kernel launch rate increased slightly.

tyler: thanks. action items
- elena: rollback kernel-priority on critical route (temp) -> elena: started PR to pin fp16 for /generate and created rollback deploy request :thumbsup:
- jonathan: add `batch_holdtime_p99` and `kv_slot_reuse_rate` to dashboards -> jonathan: pushed dashboards to staging
- siva/priya: run ablation matrix (kernel-only, jitter-only, interval-only) across 12h windows -> siva: scheduled jobs at 06:00 UTC
- tyler: follow-up with perf flamegraphs and attach to INF-7843 -> tyler: uploading now

elena: prefer cautious rollout. if canary numbers hold we can reintroduce kernel change next week with the adjusted defaults.

tyler: noted. thanks everyone. keeping thread pinned for the next 24h :eyes:
